artifacts.reason: No official Australian net / take-home pay figure exists in current official statistics for graduates or for any other population. Every official Australian earnings series published by the Australian Bureau of Statistics is GROSS. The survey that used to produce an income-after-tax measure (the Survey of Income and Housing, previously Survey of Income and Housing Costs) was discontinued after reference year 2019-20, and no successor release publishes a current net/take-home value. The Australian Taxation Office publishes tax rates, levies and 'net tax' on tax returns, but taxable income is stated after deductions rather than as gross salary, so it cannot be converted into a take-home pay figure. What was found instead is a complete published tax model (see 020_net_monthly_income.json), which satisfies the 'official gross plus complete deterministic tax model' route, but it is a derivation performed by this research, not a figure published by any Australian authority.

artifacts.reason: No single mandatory Bavarian state-wide tuition rate for non-EU Bachelor's students could be verified. (1) The Bavarian state ministry page for tuition fees is not at the assumed URL and returned HTTP 404, so no consolidated state figure was obtained. (2) Even with the two Bavarian university pages that were successfully fetched, the amounts DISAGREE (THI EUR 800/semester vs Hochschule München EUR 500/semester), which indicates the fee is set per university rather than by one uniform state rate, so there may be no single state figure to find. I am therefore not asserting a Bavarian state rate. Per-university values ARE verified and recorded separately in 007_bavaria_non_eu_tuition_thi.json (800 EUR/semester) and 008_bavaria_non_eu_tuition_hs_muenchen.json (500 EUR/semester). The enabling legal framework, Art. 13 (3) sentence 1 no. 6 BayHIG, is confirmed only indirectly via THI's own citation of it.

The widely-circulated claim that 'public universities in Germany charge no tuition for non-EU students' could NOT be confirmed from a national or federal primary source, and the fetched university evidence actively contradicts it as a general statement. Blocked/attempted: make-it-in-germany.com (the federal portal normally used for this) is behind Radware bot protection and returns no content, as warned. The Bundesministerium für Bildung und Forschung (BMBF) and the DAAD national tuition page were not reached. What WAS verified instead, from official pages: Baden-Württemberg levies EUR 1,500/semester on non-EU students via Landeshochschulgebührengesetz; Bavaria charges EUR 500-800/semester depending on the university; TUM charges usually EUR 2,000-3,000/semester. TU Berlin charges no tuition at all. Therefore the claim is not merely unsourced, it is false as a national statement. A corpus must key the German tuition metric to Land and/or institution.

artifacts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Finanzen (BMF) - Lohn- und Einkommensteuerrechner
Bundesministerium der Finanzen (BMF) - Lohn- und Einkommensteuerrechner

artifacts.reason: Official German wage tax tables that give net pay directly for a stated gross wage DO NOT EXIST and cannot be obtained for tax year 2026, because they were abolished. Established from the primary instrument, not inferred. The Bundesministerium der Finanzen publishes only Programmablaeufe (machine-calculation programmes) for wage tax, plus calculators and informational modules. The 2026 BMF navigation, which I read, lists exactly four wage-tax sections and no table: 'FAKTORVERFAHREN', 'BERECHNUNG DER LOHNSTEUER', 'ERMITTLUNG DES ZU VERSTEUERNDEN JAHRESBETRAGS' and 'ARBEITSLOHNGRENZEN'. Under BERECHNUNG DER LOHNSTEUER the only years offered are calculators (2026, 2025, 2024 Dezember, 2024 bis November, 2023 ab Juli, 2023 bis Juni, 2022, 2021), and the 2026 entry is titled 'Lohn- und Einkommensteuerrechner: Eingabeformular 2026 Lohnsteuer'. Corroborated by a secondary publisher of German wage tax tables, which I fetched and read and which states the position directly: 'Fuer den Lohnsteuerabzug gab es bis 2003 amtliche Lohnsteuertabellen von der Finanzverwaltung. Es werden nur noch Programmablaeufe zur Berechnung der Lohnsteuer veroeffentlicht. Mit den Lohnsteuerrechnern koennen Sie die Lohnsteuer stufenlos berechnen. Dennoch werden weiterhin (nicht amtliche) Lohnsteuertabellen veroeffentlicht, weil sie uebersichtlich sind und ohne maschinelle Berechnung einfach ablesbar sind.' CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS CORPUS: the ideal German evidence tier, an official tax authority publishing a net-pay table, is permanently unavailable. A net figure can only be produced by running the authority's own calculator or by implementing its Programmablaufplan, which is what DE/020_net_monthly_income.json and DE/020b_net_monthly_income_academics.json do.

artifacts.reason: No official French source publishes a take-home (net a payer) or median net monthly wage statistic for graduates, or for employees at all. Established positively, not by failure to find a page: the official French data portal INSEE publishes gross wage distributions and, for its wage statistics, publishes DECILES rather than take-home, because its wage data are collected as gross; the official income-tax authority impots.gouv.fr publishes the withholding rate grids (archived in FR/021_net_monthly_income_pas_grille_officielle.json) and a net imposable calculator, but no net a payer table; the official social security portal service-public.fr publishes employee contribution rates and bases (archived in FR/020_net_monthly_income.json) but no net a payer table. No French authority publishes a gross-to-net conversion table, so the figure the corpus holds has to be DERIVED from those two official component sets rather than quoted as a published net. The derivation is recorded in FR/020_net_monthly_income.json (net a payer EUR 2,205.69 per month from EUR 2,800.53 gross) and is usable. What does not exist is the thing this file would otherwise have supplied: an official published median take-home figure.

artifacts.publisher: The University of Auckland (Waipapa Taumata Rau)
New Zealand Legislation (Parliamentary Counsel Office) - Education (Domestic Student: Tertiary Education and Vocational Education and Training) Notice 2025, SL 2025/325
artifacts.as_of: in force from 2026-01-01; notified in Gazette 18 December 2025

artifacts.reason: DETERMINATIVE FINDING: New Zealand has NO equivalent of Australia's one-year domestic-fee cap for a second degree. I established this from the primary instrument, not from absence of evidence. The classes of persons entitled to be treated as if they are not international students for tertiary purposes are exhaustively enumerated in the Schedule to the Education (Domestic Student: Tertiary Education and Vocational Education and Training) Notice 2025 (SL 2025/325), which came into force on 1 January 2026 and revoked its predecessor. I retrieved and read that Schedule in full: it contains exactly ten clauses - diplomatic immunity; refugee/protected-person claimants and their partners and children; study under a New Zealand Government-approved exchange programme; enrolment in a Doctor of Philosophy programme at a New Zealand university; transitional TEC Industry Training Fund apprenticeships; Accredited Employer Work Visa holders on work-based Green List or sector-agreement study; TEC-funded search and rescue training; TEC English-language/adult education on partner-of-a-New-Zealander visas; and employer-required work-related training of 10 days or less. NOT ONE of the ten clauses refers to a second degree, a second qualification, a prior degree already held, a first year of a second qualification, or any time cap on paying domestic fees. The only study-concession clauses are the exchange-programme clause and the PhD clause. Consequently an international student in New Zealand who already holds one degree and enrols in another is, on the face of this instrument, an international student for the second degree and must pay international tuition - there is no domestic-fee cap and no first-year-only concession. Two important reinforcements: (1) clause 5, 'Domestic student status not transferable', forecloses the argument that a concession earned on one programme carries across to another; (2) the Ministry of Education's current guidance page (last updated 18 August 2026) confirms SL 2025/325 is the operative instrument for tertiary education, so this is the live position rather than a superseded one. WHAT REMAINS UNVERIFIED, stated precisely so the finding is not overread: the notice fixes ENTITLEMENT to domestic treatment, not tuition PRICE, and it does not rule out discretionary, institution-specific or scholarship-based fee relief awarded by a university - NZ universities do offer their own scholarships and fee-waiver schemes, but I did not fetch any university or Education Ministry funding page, so no institutional second-degree waiver is asserted. Separately, the ~NZD 10,000 per year domestic PhD fee and the NZD 56 million Crown subsidy cap that circulate in media commentary were NOT verified: they appear only in RNZ and other news snippets I did not retrieve, and the Subsidy is being reviewed, so no figure is claimed.

artifacts.reason: ICA does not publish a monetary financial-proof threshold for a Student's Pass. The pages I fetched from the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority require financial information to be supplied but state no amount. Verbatim from the ICA Institutes of Higher Learning page: 'You will need the following documents/ information to complete your Student's Pass application, please have them ready before you apply: The Registration Acknowledgement Letter from the school you plan to attend; Your travel document biodata page and birth certificate (if applicable); Your personal information, including the list of countries / places you have previously resided in, your educational background, employment history and financial support; Your parents', spouse's, and/or siblings' personal information (if applicable); Your residential address and contact details in Singapore; Your email address; Your recent, passport-sized, digital, colour photograph taken within the last three months.' The corresponding ICA form V36, surfaced in search, asks for 'Applicant Average Monthly Income for past 6 months: SGD', 'Current Saving: SGD' and 'Other financial support' amounts, which confirms ICA asks for financial data without setting a floor. Singapore does publish a per-capita income threshold, but for MOE means-tested financial aid (S$1,875 PCI for international students), not for the Student's Pass — so no such figure is reported as a visa requirement.

artifacts.reason: Singapore Permanent Residence is not conferred by a minimum number of years of study and I did not fetch an ICA or Ministry of Home Affairs page establishing any minimum-years rule, so no figure is recorded. The Student's Pass pages I did fetch say nothing about a PR route: ICA's completion-of-formalities page states only that on expiry of the Student's Pass 'you will need to get a work pass to work in Singapore.' Any PR qualification would have to be assessed under ICA's discretionary PR application process, which is not a study-length threshold and was not fetched. Recording this as UNAVAILABLE rather than inventing a minimum.

artifacts.reason: The United States has no federal proof-of-funds threshold for an F or M student visa. No federal figure was found on any government page I fetched. What is published is institution-specific: the Form I-20 is completed by the school, and the school certifies its own estimate of cost. The closest official document I could fetch confirms the opposite point — the Department of State directs students to the SEVP-approved school for the first step and to the SEVIS I-901 fee, with no money threshold stated — while the university pages I fetched state their own required total budget (for example Michigan Tech's USD 63,019 non-resident annual total, which is that institution's estimate, not a national requirement). Any specific I-20 amount must therefore be attributed to a named university rather than to the US government, and I did not fetch a university page that publishes a dedicated 'proof of funds' number separate from its cost-of-attendance budget. travel.state.gov returned HTTP 403 to every request, so the Department of State's student-visa document list could not be read directly.
